## Cognitive Agents with Dynamic Workflows

Unlike rigid automation tools like n8n or traditional LangChain agents, our LangGraph cognitive agents execute dynamic workflows that adapt to achieve objectives. They don't need pre-defined flows for each scenario—they reason, retry, and self-correct until they succeed.

## Specialized Agents

Under the hood there is not one bot but several specialists that hand the conversation between them as needed. You see a single conversation; this is what happens behind it.

### Emergency Agent

Response

Urgency specialist that automatically detects critical situations and activates immediate escalation protocols.
- Recognises urgency by what it means, not by keywords, and points to the exact sentence in the message
- Immediate escalation to a real person
- Automatic escalation to medical staff
- If something fails internally, it escalates anyway: an emergency is never lost
- Empathetic but urgent and professional tone

### Sales Agent

Hybrid RAG

Commercial advisor with hybrid search (BM25 + semantic) that finds precise information from your catalog.
- Hybrid search with cross-encoder reranking
- Only quotes prices that are in your documents: if it does not have the figure, it does not make one up
- Responses adapted to your brand tone
- Automatic purchase intent detection
- Intelligent handoff to appointment agent

### Scheduling Agent

Real calendar

24/7 booking into the business's own calendar, with an automatic copy in Google Calendar via OAuth 2.0.
- Checks real availability before offering a time
- If a booking fails halfway, it is rolled back: no half-made appointments
- Automatic copy in Google Calendar, with reminders
- Automatic confirmations via message
- Modification and cancellation without intervention

### Availability Agent

Temporal Awareness

Consultant with temporal awareness that understands "tomorrow", "next week" and verifies schedules in real time.
- Intelligent natural language date parsing
- Checks the business calendar in real time
- Automatic buffer times between appointments
- Alternative time slot suggestions
- Timezone-aware for international clients

### Support Agent

Chatwoot + RAG

Resolves frequently asked questions with RAG and automatically escalates to human agents in Chatwoot when needed.
- Knowledge base with RAG for FAQs
- Escalation detection by sentiment
- Smooth transfer to Chatwoot
- Complete conversation history
- Assignment to a person or a team in Chatwoot

### Email Marketing

Multi-Provider

Automated campaigns and follow-ups with fallback between providers (SMTP, SendGrid, Mailgun).
- Automatic post-conversation follow-ups
- Customizable HTML templates
- Multi-provider with automatic fallback
- Retry with exponential backoff
- Attachment support

### WhatsApp Campaigns

10K msgs/day

Massive automated campaigns microservice that sends up to 10,000 WhatsApp template messages per day without human intervention.
- Up to 10,000 template messages per day
- Approved WhatsApp Business templates
- Automated scheduling and queuing
- Delivery tracking and analytics
- Segmented audience targeting

## Why Choose Hachi?

Key differentiators that set us apart from traditional automation tools

#### Dynamic Workflows vs Rigid Flows

Unlike n8n or LangChain agents that follow pre-defined rigid workflows, our cognitive agents adapt dynamically to achieve objectives, retrying and self-correcting without manual intervention.

#### Instant Knowledge Updates

Upload well-structured documents and agents learn automatically via RAG. Change promotions or services instantly—no specialized support needed. Reduce maintenance time and costs dramatically.

#### Scale to Hundreds of Tools

Our tested backend architecture is ready to rapidly scale to hundreds of agents and integrations. Customer service agents are just the beginning—the platform supports any workflow type.

#### 30-Message Conversation Memory

Agents remember context from the last 30 messages per client: names, services asked, previous promotions sent. Personalized interactions that feel human and build trust.

#### Customizable Agent Prompts

Sub-prompts are fully configurable and stored in PostgreSQL per user. Customize agent personality, tone, and behavior to match your brand without touching code.

#### Smart Message Queuing

Celery workers with per-chat locks prevent simultaneous processing of messages from the same conversation, ensuring coherent responses that never lose context.

## Cutting-Edge Technology

Enterprise architecture designed for maximum performance, reliability, and scalability

#### Hybrid LangGraph Orchestration

Rule Engine for fast decisions + LLM for complex scenarios. 50+ nodes with conditional routing.

#### RAG with Hybrid Search

BM25 + semantic with adaptive alpha, cross-encoder reranking, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).

#### Native Multi-Tenant

Complete isolation per company: Redis prefixes, separate vector namespaces, independent configs.

#### Redis Shared State

SharedStateStore with typed dataclasses for pricing, scheduling, handoffs, and audit trail.

#### OAuth + Fernet Encryption

Encrypted credentials in PostgreSQL, automatic token refresh, multi-provider.

#### Celery + Redis Queue

Asynchronous webhook processing, retry with exponential backoff, no message loss.

With a €200 ticket, between 2 and 8 saved appointments a month cover the fee, depending on the plan. The calculator runs it with your numbers and tells you if it does not pay off.

#### Answers in seconds, 24/7

Also at night, at weekends and on public holidays, which is when people write most and nobody else answers.

More than 80 invariants stop the AI from confirming a taken slot, double-booking, leaving a booking half-done or inventing a price.

## Why quotes range from €29 to €900 for "the same thing"

If you are collecting quotes, you will see wildly different numbers described identically: "an AI assistant that answers WhatsApp and books appointments." They are not the same. They are three different technologies.

| You, rewriting instructions

Hachi is tier 3, and it costs less than its own tier: our most complete plan is €990/month where the market reaches €1,840, and our highest implementation fee is €1,690 where that range starts at €2,000.

When you compare €99 against €390, the question is not "why is it more expensive?" It is: what does it cost you when the €99 one confirms a slot that was already booked?

## And compared with Respond.io, Retell AI or Landbot?

They are good tools and each one wins at its own thing. This is what each does best, and what Hachi adds.

#### Respond.io

Messaging for teams

It is better if your priority is coordinating a large sales team inside the chats: advanced routing and productivity metrics per person.

Hachi adds a conversation that ends in an appointment written into your calendar with nobody stepping in, under the guardrails above. And your team steps in whenever it wants, through an inbox with assignment, teams and reports.

#### Retell AI or Vapi

Voice infrastructure

They are excellent at transcribing, speaking and handling interruptions. In fact, Hachi's voice runs on Retell. What they do not bring is the agent: with them alone you have to program who checks the calendar, what may be promised and what happens when something fails.

Hachi adds the agent already built — booking, changes, cancellations, sales and emergencies — with the same guarantees as in chat, in Spanish, English or Portuguese. Honestly: it answers in about 4 seconds on average, because it checks first; meanwhile it says a short phrase. A voice that only chats answers sooner, but checks nothing.

#### Landbot and button bots

Guided flows

They are the right choice if your whole process fits in a menu: the client taps fixed options and there is no room for misunderstanding.

Hachi adds what you look for in buttons — an AI that does not make up what matters — without forcing anyone to tap them: it understands free text and voice notes, and the critical part is enforced by code, not by the model.

## When does it pay for itself?

The most honest arithmetic we can show you: how many saved appointments per month cover the fee.

At a €400 average ticket, halve every figure. What is counted is contribution margin, not revenue: a €200 appointment is not €200 of profit.

#### No-shows

Automatic reminders cut no-shows by 40-60%. Every slot that does not sit empty is revenue you had already lost.

#### The 11pm enquiry

Someone who writes at 23:40 and hears nothing until 10:00 has already messaged three competitors. Replying in seconds is not convenience — it is the sale.

#### The ones who vanish

They asked the price and never wrote again. Proactive follow-up picks them back up on its own, without anyone having to remember.

#### The honest comparison

A receptionist in Spain costs €25,000-€35,000 a year fully loaded, and takes days off. Hachi does not replace your team: it takes off their plate what they should not be doing.

### Run it on your numbers, not ours

Put in your own ticket, appointments and no-show rate, and see the whole account: what walks out of the door with every no-show, and the reception hours that go into answering the same questions again. No sign-up, and every formula on screen.

## You do not need to be a clinic

Hachi grew up serving clinics, but what it solves is not a medical problem: it is the problem of any appointment-based business.

#### You work alone

Psychology, physiotherapy, nutrition, podiatry, therapies. One calendar, one number, and a phone buzzing while you are with someone.

#### Practice or clinic

Aesthetics, dental, spa, beauty, veterinary. Several calendars, several rooms, one overwhelmed front desk.

#### Outside healthcare

Hair, barbers, tattoo studios, photography, consultancies, academies, personal trainers. If people book a time, it fits.

#### You do not need a company

Sole trader, your own tax ID, no legal entity. The Solo plan exists exactly for that; there is no minimum below which we turn you away.

## Data protection, taken seriously

You handle personal data and, in healthcare, special-category data. This is not a checkbox.

#### Hachi never messages first

The assistant does not start conversations on its own. Proactive follow-up only acts on conversations that person opened themselves. Nobody gets a message without having written first.

#### The one exception, said out loud

Campaigns. You supply the list, and with it the responsibility for holding consent. We neither buy nor provide contact databases.

#### Paperwork in order

You are the data controller; we are the processor. We sign the Article 28 GDPR agreement before touching a single record.

#### Health data

Treated as special category (Art. 9), with the safeguards that requires. And you can exercise erasure for a specific person when they ask.

## Guardrails in code: why it cannot invent an appointment, or a price

Today the question that matters about any AI is not whether it converses well, but who is in control when it gets something wrong. This is our answer, without jargon.

A language model is persuasive even when it is wrong. If you let it decide on its own whether Thursday 17:00 is free, one day it will say yes when it is not — and the person who deals with that is your client, at your front desk.

#### The AI decides

It works out what the person wants, even in a voice note, half-finished, or with three requests in one message. That it does well, and that is what it is for.

#### The code enforces

Checking availability, writing to the calendar, not double-booking, not dropping a message: that runs on verified code. If the slot is not free, there is no booking, whatever the conversation says.

### What the code prevents, whatever the model says

#### Confirming a taken slot

It checks the real calendar before offering a time. If there is no free slot, there is no booking.

#### Double-booking

Even if the client insists three times or sends the details in pieces, the booking is created once.

#### Leaving a booking half-done

If a step fails while moving an appointment, what was done is rolled back: the old one is never left cancelled with the new one missing.

#### Booking a time that has passed

Dates are calculated by the code, in your business's time zone, not by the model.

#### Inventing a price

An amount that is not in your documents and that the client did not say is removed before sending, and it says the figure will be confirmed.

#### Posing as another business

If someone tries to make it introduce itself as another company, it does not, on the phone either.

#### Claiming to be a person

If asked, it says it is an AI assistant, as Article 50 of the EU AI Act requires.

#### Losing an emergency

Faced with an emergency or a request to speak to someone, it escalates to a person, even if something fails internally.

80+

invariants enforced in code, each with its own automated test, not entrusted to the model's instructions.

Each one answers the same question: if the model gets it wrong right here, what stops it? It is slow, unglamorous work, and it is exactly the difference between an assistant that dazzles in the demo and one that survives six months without you checking what it says.

## The WhatsApp API is not WhatsApp Business

Almost nobody explains this before you sign, and it drives the most important decision of all: your number.

|
| | WhatsApp Business app | WhatsApp API

| Where you use it | On the phone | From a computer, in the browser

| Who answers | One person | Several people at once

| Can it be automated? | Quick replies only | It is the only way

| Anything to install? | Yes, the app | No

#### Path A · New SIM

A new number for the assistant. Your usual WhatsApp stays untouched on the phone. Fastest route, nothing is lost.

#### Path B · Migrate your number

Clients keep writing to the number they know. In exchange, the history and contacts stored in the app stop being there. Meta does not allow the same number on the app and the API at once.

That history can be rescued before migrating. It is not automation: it is database work, and we quote it separately. We say so now, not once there is no way back.

## Frequently asked questions

The ones we get most, answered without hedging.

### How much does Hachi cost?

Six options: Pay-per-booking, €49/month plus €4 per appointment booked over chat and €9 per call, capped at €990; Solo, €149/month; Essential, €390/month; Professional, €690/month; Complete, €990/month; and Multi-site from €1,690/month. On top there is a one-off implementation fee of €290 to €1,690 depending on the plan, charged only if you decide to continue after the trial.

### Does it answer phone calls? On which plan?

Yes. AI voice reception, which checks the calendar and books during the call, is included from the Professional plan (400 minutes a month). On Solo and Essential it is an optional add-on for €190/month with 300 minutes. The €149 plan does not include voice on its own.

### Is the demo free? Do you ask for a card?

Free, and no card. First a video call where we show it working, then 7 days of trial with your assistant already configured. If you do not continue, you pay nothing.

### Will it message my patients without permission?

No. Hachi does not start conversations. Follow-up only acts on conversations that person opened themselves. The exception is campaigns, where you supply the list and are responsible for holding consent.

### Can it confirm an appointment that does not exist?

No, because the booking is not decided by the language model. Availability checks and calendar writes run on verified code. If the slot is not free, there is no appointment.

### What happens if the AI gets it wrong?

What matters does not depend on it. More than 80 critical rules are enforced in code: it does not confirm a taken slot, does not double-book, does not leave a booking half-done, does not quote a price that is not in your documents, does not pose as another business, does not claim to be a person and, in an emergency, escalates to someone on your team. The model understands and converses; the code enforces.

### Can I keep my usual number?

Yes, but decide it with the facts in front of you. Meta does not allow the same number on the WhatsApp Business app and the API at the same time. Either you use a new SIM, or you migrate your usual one accepting that the history stored in the app stops being accessible. It can be rescued beforehand, quoted separately.

### How long until it is running?

Three to five working days once we have your details and the number question settled. We do the setup; you build nothing.

### What if I exceed my plan's conversations?

Service is not cut off. Extra conversations bill at €0.25 each and extra call minutes at €0.20. If the overage is constant we suggest moving plan, because it works out cheaper for you.

### Is there a lock-in period?

No. You can leave whenever you want. Implementation is charged once on signing, and is waived if you pay a quarter up front.

### Does it replace my receptionist?

No, and anyone who says otherwise is selling you smoke. It takes the repetitive part off their plate — opening hours, prices, directions, moving an appointment — so their time goes where a person is actually needed. And it covers nights and weekends, when there is nobody.

## For readers who came for the architecture

If you got this far looking for engineering rather than pricing, this part is for you.

#### Neuro-symbolic architecture

Graph nodes emit typed signals that a router with no LLM in the loop turns into flow decisions. The model proposes; the state machine disposes. Check-Signal-Act in every node.

#### Guarded invariants

More than 80 properties the system guarantees in code, with an explicit cut-off rule: if Python guarantees the outcome it is an invariant; if only the prompt asks for it, it is a suggestion.

#### Real multi-tenancy

Per-tenant isolation down to the conversation checkpointer key. Every query is parameterised and scoped by tenant: one client's state cannot leak into another's.

#### Agents that build themselves

The graph can be compiled from the database: a new agent is defined with typed extraction fields and its own tools, with no code deploy.

#### Idempotency and compensation

Safe retry across the whole external surface. A duplicated webhook does not create two appointments; a retried campaign does not send twice.

#### Multi-provider inference

The inference layer is decoupled: provider and model are selected per tenant. No dependency on a single vendor or a single model family.

#### What that means in money

The variable cost of serving one client — messaging, inference and telephony — is measured in tens of euros per month, against fees of €390 to €990. Margin does not depend on scaling headcount, because maintaining the assistant is autonomous: there are no flows to redraw when a business changes its prices or its hours.

And the moat is not the model, which anyone can rent. It is the slow work of turning more than 80 critical behaviours into verifiable guarantees. That does not get replicated in a weekend with a flow builder.

Investing, or building things like this? Write to ceo@hachi.live with "technical" or "investment" in the subject and I will answer personally.

# An AI receptionist that speaks your industry's language

The problem is the same everywhere — people call and text when you cannot pick up — but the words, the emergencies and what gets booked change. These pages show how Hachi works in each one, with a sample conversation and the maths on how many bookings it takes to pay for itself.

For businesses in the United States

## Where we do not fit, said up front

Hachi books appointments and visits into a calendar with slots. So it is not the tool for restaurants (table reservations run on their own systems), hotels (they need a booking engine) or for routing technicians across town. If that is your business, we will tell you in the demo.

## Is your industry missing?

If you work by appointment, it almost certainly fits. Tell us about yours in the demo and we will show you a conversation with your own services.

Title: ROI calculator: what no-shows really cost | Hachi

# What a schedule that falls apart actually costs

Two calculations using your figures: what you lose to no-shows,
and what goes into answering the same messages over and over. No sign-up, and
every formula on screen.

How to read this. You supply your clinic's figures, because only
you know them. The one thing that has to be assumed is marked in amber, with a
slider and the most conservative value preselected: if it looks
optimistic to you, drag it down and watch what happens. The result changes in front
of you.

## 1 · What no-shows cost you

A patient who doesn't turn up leaves a slot that is already paid for: the room,
the equipment and the practitioner are still there. What you lose is that
appointment's margin.

Careful with this number: freeing hours is not automatically
saving money. If nobody stops working, what you gain is capacity
— those hours go somewhere else — and it is worth whatever that something else
generates. It only turns into cash when it avoids a hire, cuts contracted hours,
or removes overtime.

## 3 · Result on your plan

Adding the two is legitimate because they measure different things: one is
revenue you were losing, the other is cost you were spending. No double counting.

## 4 · If the assumption falls short

The only arguable figure is how many no-shows a reminder prevents. Here is what
happens if it turns out worse than expected.

| | No-shows avoided | New appointments | Margin | Net after fee

### Where each number comes from

### Why contribution margin and not revenue

A recovered €200 appointment is not €200 of profit: it consumes product,
consumables and, where applicable, the practitioner's commission. Only the
margin is incremental profit. Presenting gross revenue as "savings" is the most
common mistake in calculators like this, and the first thing an analyst spots.

In favour of the calculation: fixed costs — the room, the equipment, the
practitioner already on site — are already paid in that slot.
That is precisely why contribution margin, not net margin, is the right measure.

### Why slots you already refill are subtracted

Almost no clinic loses 100% of its no-shows: some get rebooked by phone or from
a waiting list. If you already refill 25%, only 75% of what is avoided is
new revenue. Without this term the result is overstated by 20–40%.

### How the hourly cost is calculated

Not gross salary divided by contracted hours. It is the fully loaded cost:
salary × (1 + payroll overhead) ÷ effective hours.
- Employer payroll overhead (~32%): the default is Spain's general
regime — common contingencies 23.60% · unemployment 5.50% · wage guarantee
fund 0.20% · vocational training 0.60% · MEI ~0.75% · occupational accident
rate by activity. This figure varies a lot by country
(roughly 8% in the UK, 13% in Ireland, 20% in Italy), which is why the field
is editable — set yours.
- Effective hours: 1,700 per year. Not contracted hours (1,780–1,826
under Spanish collective agreements, holidays already deducted): real
absence has to be subtracted. Using contracted hours understates the hourly
cost — and since a high hourly cost favours the argument here, the
conservative value is used.

### The 40–60% range

This is the effect attributed to reminders with confirmation: the patient either
confirms or cancels in time, and the slot can be reassigned. The default applies
40%, the low end. It is an assumption, not a promise — which is
why it sits on a slider instead of being buried in the code.

### What this calculator does NOT count

All of this adds up, but cannot be backed by arithmetic, so it stays out:
- The lifetime value of a patient who never comes back after a no-show.
- The opportunity cost of an idle room beyond the ticket.
- The reputational effect of a schedule that works.
- Out-of-hours enquiries currently answered the next morning.

Leaving value out is what makes the value left in believable.

Title: FAQ · Pricing, channels, booking and GDPR | Hachi

# Everything people ask before buying

85 questions answered in full, including the ones that argue against us:
what you lose by migrating your number, when Hachi is not worth it,
and the case in which a €29 tool is the right decision.

No question matches that text.

Write to us and we will answer it: contact form.

## What Hachi is, and who it is for

The basics: what it does, what it does not do, and whether it fits your business.

### What exactly is Hachi?#

An AI assistant that answers your WhatsApp around the clock,
checks your real calendar and books the appointment. Then it sends
the reminders, and if someone asked and went quiet, it writes back.

The difference from most of the market is one verb: it does not only
converse, it also executes against your calendar.

### Is it a chatbot?#

Not in the usual sense. A menu chatbot makes you press "1 to book, 2 for prices"
and breaks the moment you type something it was not expecting. Hachi understands
free language, in text and in voice notes, and when a conversation turns delicate it
flags someone on your team instead of improvising.

### Does it replace my receptionist?#

No, and we do not sell it that way. It takes the repetitive part off their plate —
prices, opening hours, location, parking, what to do beforehand — which is 80% of the
messages. Your team spends its time on whoever is actually in the building, which is
where the difference shows.

### I am not a clinic. Does it still work for me?#

Yes. Hachi is not built for a sector, it is built for a problem: people message you
when you cannot answer, and by the time you do it is too late.

It works for hair and barber shops, tattoo studios, vets, garages, academies,
photography, consultancies and practices. The vocabulary changes — where it says
"patient" it will say "client" — and so does your list of services. Nothing else.

### I work alone, with no team. Does it make sense for me?#

That is precisely where it shows most, because there is no front desk to absorb the
messages: either you answer or nobody does. The
Solo plan (€149/month) exists for exactly that — one calendar, one
number — and there is no minimum below which we turn you away.

### Do I need to be a registered company?#

No. We invoice sole traders against their own tax ID without any problem, and the
invoice carries Spanish VAT and is deductible like any other supplier's.

### When does Hachi NOT make sense?#

We would rather say it than sell you something you will not use. It does not pay
off if you do not work by appointment, if you receive
very few messages a month (losing three messages does not cover a
subscription), or if WhatsApp is not your channel because you sell
in a shop or over the phone.

### Which sectors do you have the most experience in?#

Aesthetic medicine — the main one — dental practices, spa and wellness, and other
health and therapy practices: physiotherapy, nutrition, psychology, podiatry, speech
therapy. Also solo professionals and appointment-based businesses outside healthcare.
The list is where we have flying hours, not who we accept.

### Which languages does it speak?#

Spanish, English and Portuguese. There are no menus and no "press 1":
it answers in the language the person writes or speaks in, including when they switch
halfway through a conversation or a call.

Your data does not change: the names of your services, your prices and your
business name stay exactly as they are. Only the reply is translated.

## Pricing, plans and billing

All figures in euros, VAT not included, and no lock-in.

### How much does Hachi cost per month?#

Six options: Pay-per-booking, €49 plus €4 per appointment booked
over chat and €9 per appointment booked during a call, capped at €990;
Solo €149, Essential €390,
Professional €690, Complete €990 and
Multi-site from €1,690 a month. No lock-in: the fee is monthly and
you can leave whenever you want.

AI voice calls are included from the Professional plan; on Solo and Essential they
are an add-on at €190/month.

They are laid out in detail on the pricing section.

### What does each plan include?#
- Pay-per-booking (€49 + €4 per chat booking and €9 per call booking,
capped at €990) — unlimited conversations and reminders, no proactive
follow-up or campaigns.
- Solo (€149) — WhatsApp 24/7, real calendar, cancellations and
rescheduling, reminders, 250 conversations/month. No voice: it can be added for
€190/month with 300 minutes.
- Essential (€390) — the above plus several calendars or
practitioners, full dashboard with metrics, 750 conversations/month.
- Professional (€690) — plus phone handling with an AI voice that
books during the call and WhatsApp calls, 1,500 conversations and 400 minutes.
- Complete (€990) — plus proactive follow-up, WhatsApp campaigns
and outbound calls, 3,000 conversations and 800 minutes.
- Multi-site (from €1,690) — several sites in one account, your
own branding, and reselling.

### Is there a plan that charges per booking instead of per conversation?#

Yes, the Pay-per-booking plan: a €49/month base fee, plus
€4 for each appointment Hachi books over chat and €9
for each one it books during a call. Conversations are unlimited: talking is free, only
bookings are charged.

Reminders are included and there is a monthly cap of €990, the fee
of the Complete plan. Implementation is €290. Proactive follow-up and campaigns are not
included, because they work when nobody is writing and their cost does not depend on
bookings. If two months in a row it costs you more than a fixed plan, we tell you and
switch you.

### Can I have voice calls without moving to the Professional plan?#

Yes. On the Solo and Essential plans, voice is an optional add-on at €190/month
with 300 minutes included (extra minutes at €0.20). From the Professional plan
it is included: 400 minutes, and 800 on Complete.

The €149 plan does not include voice on its own: with the add-on, the fee comes to
€339 a month.

### Is there a setup fee?#

Yes, a one-off charge from €290 to €1,690 depending on the plan —
under two months of fee in every case. It covers loading your services, prices and
durations, connecting your WhatsApp number and your calendar, configuring your real
opening hours, tuning your brand's tone and training your team.

It is not charged until you decide to continue after the free
trial, and it is waived entirely if you pay a quarter up front.

### When do I pay for the first time?#

At the end, and only if you say yes. In order: the demo video call costs
€0, configuring your assistant €0, the 7-day trial
€0. If you decide to continue, that is when setup (once) and the
first monthly fee appear. If you decide not to, €0. No card is asked
for to run the trial.

### How many saved appointments a month does it take to pay for itself?#

At a €200 average ticket and a 65% contribution margin: 2
appointments for Solo, 3 for Essential, 6 for Professional and 8 for Complete. At a
€400 ticket, halve each figure.

Margin is counted rather than revenue on purpose: a €200 appointment is not €200
of profit, because it consumes product and consumables. You can run the maths on your
own numbers in the ROI calculator.

### What counts as a "conversation"?#

One customer talking to you across 24 hours, not each message. If
somebody sends thirty messages in an afternoon sorting out their questions and
booking, that is one conversation.

Which is why the allowances go further than they look: a clinic receiving "20
messages a day" usually lands at 150-250 conversations a month, not 600.

### What happens if I go over the plan limit?#

The service is not cut off. No customer of yours goes unanswered
for having hit a cap: that would be the opposite of what you bought.

Conversations beyond the plan are billed at €0.25 each and call
minutes at €0.20, itemised line by line on the invoice. If you go
over two months running we tell you and suggest moving up a plan, which is almost
always cheaper than paying the excess.

### Why is there a conversation limit at all?#

It is not an artificial cap to push you upmarket. Every reply consumes AI
processing charged by usage; the WhatsApp provider charges per message; and there is
hosting, history storage and human maintenance work behind it.

One detail almost nobody states correctly: replying within 24 hours of the
customer's message costs Meta nothing. What is paid for are the messages we
initiate — reminders and campaigns. The limit sizes the service; it does not cover a
Meta tariff.

### Can I change plan?#

Yes, up or down whenever you like; it applies from the next invoice. Not getting it
right at first is normal: we start from your estimate and after two months there is
real data from your business to tune it.

### Is there a lock-in?#

No. The fee is monthly and cancellation is requested before the renewal date, with
no penalty. There is a discount only if you choose to pay quarterly.

### How do I pay and what invoice do I get?#

Credit or debit card, SEPA direct debit or PayPal, always in euros:
no currency conversion fee and no international charge appears on your statement.

You receive a deductible invoice with Spanish VAT, made out to your company or your
sole-trader tax ID, issued automatically each month. If you have an intra-EU VAT
number, the payment gateway applies whatever is due once you enter it.

### Can I resell Hachi under my own brand?#

Yes, that is the Multi-site / White Label plan, from €1,690/month.
Several sites or businesses in one account without mixing, the dashboard and
communications under your brand, unlimited custom agents and priority support. You
decide what to charge each of your own clients: the margin is yours.

The final price depends on the number of sites and the volume, so it is worked out
case by case on a call.

## The demo and the trial

Two different things, and both are free. It is the most common confusion.

### What is the difference between the demo and the trial?#

The demo is 20 minutes on a video call, watching it with us. The
trial is 7 days using it yourself, with your real customers. First
one, then the other, and the first payment only if you decide to stay.

### Is the demo free? Do you ask for a card?#

Free and with no commitment, and no payment details are requested. Nor for starting
the 7-day trial.

### How long does the demo last?#

Twenty minutes. We show you Hachi handling a WhatsApp conversation, checking the
calendar and closing a real appointment, and sending a reminder. We answer your
questions and work out which plan fits you.

### During the trial, is it a simulation or does it really handle customers?#

It really does. Beforehand we set your assistant up with your services, your prices,
your number and your calendar — 3 to 5 working days — and for those 7 days it handles
your actual customers. You see every conversation, every appointment booked and every
reminder sent.

### Only 7 days of trial? Others give a month#

Seven days with your business genuinely running is enough to see it clearly. And we
will be straight about the reason: we do not give you a toy demo, we build the whole
assistant, and that is days of our team's work before the trial starts. A free
month would mean doing that work for nothing many times over, and we would end up
covering it by raising the price for everyone.

### If I am not convinced when the trial ends, what do I pay?#

Nothing. Not the configuration, not the setup fee, not the subscription. Nothing is
charged until you decide to continue.

### How do I book a demo?#

From the contact form on this site, or by messaging on
WhatsApp. Outside business hours the assistant itself handles you and books it — which
is, incidentally, the best demonstration available.

## WhatsApp: the API, your number and the 24-hour window

The part the industry explains worst, and the one that causes the most grief when it surfaces late.

### What is the difference between WhatsApp Business and WhatsApp Business API?#

They are two different products. The app — the free one on your
phone — is built for a business that replies. The API is
Meta's official route for companies that also message first and work at
volume.
- Where it runs: the app on a phone; the API on a computer, in a
web console.
- Who replies: in the app, one person by hand; on the API, your
team and the assistant at once.
- Messaging first: in the app, risk of a block; on the API,
allowed with an approved template.
- History: in the app, only on that phone; on the API,
centralised and searchable.

The whole thing is laid out in
WhatsApp Business vs API.

### Why can my number be blocked for using the normal WhatsApp Business?#

Because the app is not built for starting conversations. Once you begin sending
messages to people who did not write to you that day, or many in a row, WhatsApp reads
it as spam: first it throttles your sending, then it suspends the number temporarily,
and if it repeats, it blocks it permanently.

And that number is usually the one you have had for years, the one
on your Google listing, your website and your cards.

### Can I keep my existing number?#

Yes, but it is worth deciding deliberately, because one Meta rule governs everything:
a number can be on the WhatsApp Business app OR on the API, never on both at
once.

There are two paths and they are set out in the next two questions.

### Path A: a new number. What does it involve?#

A new SIM for the API. Your existing WhatsApp Business stays untouched on
the phone, with all its chats and contacts. Zero risk, and ready in the same
time frame as the rest of the setup.

The catch: it is a different number from the one on your website, your Google
listing and your cards, so you have to start promoting it or set up a redirect. It is
what we recommend to almost everyone, especially if your current WhatsApp has years of
history in it.

### Path B: migrating my number. Do I lose the history and contacts?#

Yes, and this is what almost nobody mentions until it is too late:
when a number moves to the API, the chat history and contacts living in the
phone app stop being accessible. The API starts clean. That number stops
working in the app, and with it goes access to those conversations from the new
console.

Anyone who tells you "don't worry, we'll just connect your WhatsApp Business" is not
telling you this. You would find out the day you go looking for a customer conversation
from eight months ago.

### Can the old data be rescued before migrating?#

Yes, but it has to happen before migrating and it is separate work:
extracting the contact list and conversation history, organising them and loading them
into the new system.

That is not automation, it is database work: done case by case depending on how many
contacts and how much history you have, which is why it is quoted
separately after looking at what is there. We tell you before we start, never
after.

### How do I choose between a new number and migrating?#

Two questions:
- Is the number you use now published on your website, your Google listing
and your ads? If it is not, take a new number and stop thinking about
it.
- Do you need to keep reading old conversations? If you never look
at them, migrate without a rescue. If you consult them often, the rescue is worth
it.

### What is the 24-hour window?#

Meta allows free messaging to a person for the
24 hours after their last message. After that you cannot send free
text: only a template approved by Meta in advance.

Day to day: someone messages at 22:00 and Hachi replies with complete freedom for
the next 24 hours. If they do not write again for three days and you want to follow up,
they are outside the window, so the message goes out as an approved template; as soon
as they reply, a fresh window opens and the conversation is unrestricted again.

### Do I have to keep track of the 24-hour window?#

No. The system knows whether the person is inside or outside the window and picks
between free message and template on its own. We prepare and submit the templates you
need — reminders, follow-ups, campaigns; Meta usually approves them within 24 to 48
hours.

This is, incidentally, why a home-made bot eventually fails: without the official API
and template handling, the message simply does not go out.

## How appointments get booked

The part that separates an assistant that converses from one that also executes.

### Does it really check my calendar before proposing a time?#

Yes, always. It never offers a time without having looked at your real availability,
and if there is no slot it proposes alternatives that do exist.

It is the question that separates the three market tiers: a drawn flow
cannot check your calendar. It is not doing it badly, it has no way of doing
it. The mechanism is explained in
why flow-based bots fail.

### Can it confirm an appointment that does not actually exist?#

No. That check is code that runs every time, not an instruction written into a prompt
that the model might skip on an odd day. It is exactly the difference you are paying for
against a €29 offer.

### If the customer insists three times, do I end up with three appointments?#

No. The details arrive in pieces — "Thursday"… "at 11"… "I'm Marta"… the phone number
at the end — and an ordinary automation either starts over on each new message or creates
a duplicate. Hachi understands it is still the same booking and completes it without
duplicating.

### What happens if a booking fails halfway?#

It undoes itself. If rescheduling cancels the old appointment and creating the new one
fails, the system reverts the change rather than leaving it half-done. Your customer does
not end up without an appointment because of an internal error.

### Can it cancel and reschedule without my team stepping in?#

Yes, both, and the calendar ends up updated. Nobody has to finish the job by hand.

### Does it work with several calendars or practitioners?#

Yes, from the Essential plan: independent calendars per site or per practitioner, each
with its own hours, services and durations. The assistant knows which one an appointment
belongs to. Duration, preparation time and deposit are configurable per service.

### Does it remember what I already told it?#

Yes, across days, not just within one message. If you already gave your name it will
not ask again, and if you said you were interested in a particular service it still has
that twenty messages later. A menu chatbot makes you repeat everything, which is exactly
what makes people give up.

### Can it book over the phone, not just on WhatsApp?#

Yes, from the Professional plan, or with the voice add-on (€190/month) on Solo and
Essential. If nobody picks up at the front desk, Hachi does, with
a natural voice, checks real availability and closes the appointment during the
call itself. Every call is logged with its transcript and summary in the
dashboard.

### What does the voice sound like and how long does it take to answer on the phone?#

A natural voice, not a robotic one. Underneath it runs on Retell AI, one
of the leading voice engines, which handles listening, speaking and the caller
interrupting. On top of it sits the Hachi agent, which checks the calendar and books
exactly as it does on WhatsApp, with the same guarantees.

Honestly: when it has to check something, it answers in about 4 seconds on
average, and meanwhile it says a short phrase such as "give me a second". A
voice that only chats answers sooner, but it does not look at your calendar. And if the
caller switches language mid-call, it switches too.

### What stops the AI from getting the important things wrong?#

The important things do not depend on the model. Hachi separates two jobs:
the AI understands and converses, and the code enforces
the critical rules — the guardrails. More than 80 are enforced this way, each with its own
automated test. Among other things, the code prevents it from:
- confirming a slot that is already taken;
- double-booking, even if the client insists or sends the details in pieces;
- leaving a booking half-done if a step fails;
- booking a time that has already passed;
- quoting a price that is not in your documents;
- introducing itself as another business;
- claiming to be a person: if asked, it says it is an AI assistant;
- losing an emergency or a request to speak to someone: it hands it to your team,
even if something fails internally.

## No-shows, follow-up and campaigns

What happens before and after the appointment, which is where the money leaks.

### How does it reduce no-shows?#

With automatic reminders before each appointment — say a week, 24 hours and 2 hours
before; you decide how many and when. The customer confirms or cancels by replying to the
reminder and the calendar updates itself.

The point is not only that more people turn up: it is that whoever cancels
does so in time, and that slot can be sold again instead of being lost.

### How much do no-shows actually drop?#

The effect attributed to reminders with confirmation sits in the
40% to 60% range. We use 40% — the low end — in every calculation we
publish, and in the calculator that number is on a slider
so you can drag it down and see what happens. It is an assumption, not a promise.

### What is proactive follow-up?#

If someone asked about a service and disappeared, Hachi writes back a few days later
with a message tailored to what they asked about. It is not a generic nudge: it picks the
conversation up where it stopped. Available from the Complete plan.

It is by a distance the most expensive thing that happens to an appointment-based
business: they ask the price, think about it, and never come back.

### Will Hachi message people who have never written to me?#

No, and it is not a sales promise: it is how the thing is built. The
assistant only replies to people who wrote first, and follow-up acts solely on
conversations that person opened themselves. If someone has never messaged you, Hachi has
no way to contact them.

The first message always comes from your customer. Hachi resumes conversations, it does
not start them. The one exception is the campaigns you launch to your own list.

### What are WhatsApp campaigns?#

Sends to your customer base using official Meta-approved templates — not irregular bulk
messaging — segmentable by customer type, service or last visit. Available from the
Complete plan.

And the important part: whoever replies goes straight into a conversation with
the assistant, which answers their questions and books them. Sending the promotion
is easy; the hard part is handling the fifty who reply at once.

### Does it classify conversations?#

Yes, on its own: interested in a particular service, appointment booked, awaiting reply,
former customer. Your team can open it and see at a glance what needs attention, and those
same labels are used to segment campaigns.

## Comparing quotes: why some cost €99 and others €900

We lay it out in full even where it argues against us, because it is the only way for you to compare properly.

### Why is there such a price gap between one offer and another?#

Because under the same description — "an AI assistant that answers your WhatsApp and
books appointments" — sit three different technologies:
- Tier 1 · Drawn flows (€29-199/month). A hand-made diagram. It does
not understand, it matches patterns. Its limit is not quality, it is capability:
it cannot check your calendar.
- Tier 2 · Assistants that converse (€150-500/month). Real AI: it
understands, informs, qualifies. What it lacks is execution: it ends with
"a colleague will confirm your appointment".
- Tier 3 · Systems that converse AND execute (€460-1,840/month). They
check real availability, book, cancel, reschedule and answer for the result.
Hachi is here.

The full breakdown is in
what an AI assistant costs.

### What four questions should I ask any quote?#

Ours included. If the person selling cannot answer them concretely, you are looking at
tier 1 or 2:
- Does it check real availability before proposing a time, or does it only look like
it does?
- If a booking fails halfway, does it stay half-done or undo itself?
- Can it book the same appointment twice if the customer insists?
- When it does not know something, does it say so or make it up?

### If Hachi is tier 3, why does it cost less than its tier?#

Because we would rather grow with customers who stay. Every plan sits below its tier's
range: the most complete is €990/month when the tier-3 market reaches €1,840, and the
highest setup fee is €1,690 when that range starts at €2,000.

What we will not do is compete with tier 1 on price.

### When is tier 1 the right choice?#

If all you need is to answer four common questions and you book nothing, a drawn flow is
plenty and it is the sensible call. We would say so either way — it is a cheaper tool that
does a different job well.

### What about automation tools like Zapier, Make or n8n?#

Those tools chain fixed steps: if A happens, do B. They are excellent for mechanical
tasks. A conversation with a customer is not one: there are questions, changes of mind,
objections and missing details that arrive in pieces.

### Hachi or Respond.io?#

It depends on what you want to solve. Respond.io is a messaging platform
for teams: it shines at routing chats among many agents and measuring their
productivity. If your priority is coordinating a large sales team inside WhatsApp, it is
a very good choice.

Hachi is built so the conversation ends in an appointment written
into your calendar with nobody stepping in, with the critical rules enforced in code.
Your team is not left out: it works from a shared inbox with conversation assignment,
teams, labels and response-time reports.

### Why not use Retell AI or Vapi directly?#

Because they are infrastructure, not an agent. Retell AI and Vapi are
excellent at transcribing, speaking and handling interruptions — in fact, Hachi's voice
runs on Retell — but with them alone you have to program who checks the calendar, what
may be promised to the client and what happens when something fails. That usually takes
a developer.

Hachi gives you that work done: several specialised agents — booking, changes,
cancellations, sales and emergencies — already built, with the same guarantees on the
phone as in chat, in Spanish, English or Portuguese, and set up by us.

### Hachi or a button bot like Landbot?#

If your whole process fits in a menu, a button bot is a sound choice: the client taps
fixed options and there is no room for misunderstanding. What you lose is everything
else: voice notes, messages that mix several requests, questions nobody anticipated.

Hachi gets you what you want from buttons — an AI that does not make up what matters
— without forcing anyone to tap them: it understands free text and voice notes, and the
critical parts (availability, the booking, prices) are enforced by code, not by the
model.

### Can it invent a price or a service I do not offer?#

An unconstrained model fills in what it does not know, because that is what it was
trained to do: it sounds convincing and it is false. In Hachi the answer is checked against
your real information before it is sent, and if the fact is missing, it
says so and offers to hand the conversation to a person.

This is not a theoretical worry: companies have been ordered to compensate customers for
what their chatbot promised.

### I already tried a chatbot and it was a disaster. Why would this be different?#

It is the most common thing we hear, and fairly: menu chatbots frustrate people. Which is
why the trial is 7 days with your real services and prices, before deciding anything. If it
does not convince you, you do not continue and you do not pay.

### It is expensive for my business#

Against hiring someone to handle WhatsApp mornings, afternoons, nights and weekends, it is
a fraction: a receptionist in Spain costs €25,000 to €35,000 a year fully
loaded, and takes days off.

And if the numbers genuinely do not work, we say so. Run them yourself in the
calculator: it is built to tell you it does not pay for
itself yet, and if that is the answer, it says so.

## Data protection and GDPR

You handle personal data and, in healthcare, special-category data. This is not a checkbox.

### Who is the controller and who is the processor?#

You are the controller: they are your customers and your data, and you
decide what they are used for. Hachi is the processor: we handle that data
on your behalf, only to provide the service, following your instructions.

### Do you sign a data processing agreement?#

Yes, the one required by Article 28 of the GDPR, before we start. It
details what data is processed, with which providers, where it is hosted and how long it is
kept. If your legal advisers need to review it or add conditions, send it over and we look at
it before signing. That is routine.

### Can Hachi send messages without consent?#

No. The assistant only replies to people who wrote first. The sole exception is campaigns
you launch, and there the rules are: you supply the list (Hachi does not buy,
scrape or infer numbers), the consent is yours as controller of that data, and
Meta also polices it by requiring an approved template. If Meta rejects it, it
does not go out.

Our recommendation: only send campaigns to people who gave you their number so you could
write to them, and keep a record of when and how.

### I handle health data. Does that change anything?#

It is special category data (Art. 9 GDPR) and deserves more care, not less.
Which is why Hachi works with the conversation — what the customer writes to request an
appointment — and does not need your clinical records: there is nothing to
upload. The less data that goes in, the better, and what is stored and for how long can be
restricted.

### What happens if one of my customers exercises their rights?#

Access, rectification, erasure, objection and portability: you pass it to us and we handle it
within the legal deadline, including complete deletion of their data and
conversations.

### Where is the data stored and for how long?#

Server location, the specific list of providers involved, exact retention periods and
international transfers are all detailed in the data processing agreement, handed over and
signed before we start. If you need to see it before deciding, ask for it at the demo.

### Are you ISO 27001 or SOC 2 certified?#

No, and we would rather say so plainly: Hachi does not currently hold certifications such
as ISO 27001 or SOC 2, which large corporations often require in procurement.

What there is: the Article 28 GDPR data processing agreement, signed before any data
is touched; health data treated as a special category; full isolation between
businesses; encrypted credentials; and the notice that the client is talking to an AI,
as required by Article 50 of the EU AI Act. If your company needs a specific
certification to buy, tell us in the demo.

### Do I lose control of what the assistant says?#

The opposite. From the dashboard you edit how it replies, what prices it quotes, what services
it offers and what it must never say. Your team sees every conversation in real
time and can step in at any moment.

### What if a customer notices it is an assistant and is put off?#

It speaks naturally and in your brand's tone. And the moment a conversation turns delicate — an
emergency, a serious complaint, someone asking for a human — it alerts your team and hands over
with the full context. Nobody gets trapped talking to a machine.

## Implementation, requirements and support

What you need to have, how long it takes and what happens afterwards.

### How long until it is up and running?#

Three to five working days from when you send your list of services and
prices. The 7-day trial starts as soon as it is built.

### What do you need from me?#
- A decision about the number: new SIM or migrating your existing one. If you
do not have WhatsApp Business API yet, we arrange it.
- Your list of services and prices, exactly as you give it to a customer. A
PDF, a spreadsheet or even screenshots: we structure it.
- Your opening hours and how many appointments fit per slot.
- Your business details: exact address, what you do offer and what you
don't.

### Do I have to install anything or change my practice-management software?#

Nothing to install — the API runs in a browser — no need to change management software, no need
for anyone to watch a phone, and no need for anyone on your team to be technical.

Hachi can work with its own calendar or sync with the one you already use; we look at that in the
demo, depending on your software.

### Is maintenance charged separately?#

No, it is included in the fee. Price changes as often as needed, adding or removing services and
durations, changes to hours, calendars, practitioners and holidays, adjustments to how the agents
behave, changes to reminders, and every platform improvement. There is no surprise
invoice each time you change something.

### Can I change things myself?#

Yes: prices, wording, hours and each agent's behaviour are all in the dashboard, and there is a
simulator for testing any change in a practice conversation before a real customer
sees it. If you would rather we did it, message us and routine changes are done within 24-48 working
hours.

### Can my team step in and split the conversations between them?#

Yes. Every conversation arrives in a shared inbox where your team sees it
in real time and can step in at any moment. You can assign each conversation to a person
or a team, use labels and canned responses, and see response-time reports.

When Hachi detects that a person is needed — an emergency, a complaint, someone asking
for it — it leaves the conversation pending for your team, with all the context.

### What is quoted separately?#

Only two things: custom integrations with management software that is not already supported, and
bespoke development that is not part of the product. In both cases you get a fixed quote before
anything is built. Plus rescuing contacts and history if you choose to migrate your number.

### What happens if something breaks?#

We monitor the service automatically and find out before you do. A serious incident — the assistant
not responding, the WhatsApp connection dropping — is handled immediately during working hours.
Multi-site plans have priority support.

### How do I check it is working?#

The dashboard shows every appointment Hachi booked, every reminder sent and every conversation
recovered, plus the service status. Nothing has to be taken on faith: the numbers are there.

### What are your opening hours?#

Sales hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 19:00 (mainland Spain time) and
Saturdays 10:00 to 14:00. Outside those hours the assistant itself handles you and
books the demo.

## Is your question missing?

Write to us and we will answer it for your specific case. And if you want
numbers rather than answers, the calculator runs the maths on yours.

Language: en
Title: What an AI assistant for clinics costs | Hachi

# What an AI assistant for clinics costs

If you are collecting quotes you will find figures from €29 to well over
€900 a month, all described the same way. They are not the same thing: they are three
different technologies. Here is what you pay for in each — including the part that
argues against us.

Updated 2026-08-05

## The spread is not about quality, it is about category

When two offers are described identically and sit €800 apart, the first thought is that
someone is padding the price. Sometimes they are. But what usually sits underneath is
that they are selling different things under the same name.

| | Tier | What it is | Per month | Setup

| 1 | Drawn flows: if they tap this button, say this | €29 – €199 | €0 – €300

| 2 | Assistants that converse but do not execute | €150 – €500 | €0 – €1,000

| 3 | Systems that converse and execute against your calendar | €460 – €1,840 | €2,000 – €15,000

The border between tier 2 and tier 3 is a single verb: execute. A
tier-2 assistant holds an excellent conversation and finishes with "a colleague will
confirm your appointment". The customer had a good experience and your team has exactly
the same work still waiting.

## What you are paying for at each tier

### Tier 1 · €29 to €199 a month

A hand-drawn diagram. You pay for the tool that lets you draw it and for the hosting. It
is cheap because there is little to maintain: no language model burning usage, no
integration with your calendar, nobody tuning anything.

When it is the right call: if all you need is to answer four common
questions and you book nothing, this is plenty and it is the most sensible thing you can
do with the money. We would say so either way.

### Tier 2 · €150 to €500 a month

Here there is genuine AI, and that costs: every reply consumes processing charged by
usage. You are paying for natural-language understanding, not for the ability to act.

### Tier 3 · €460 to €1,840 a month

Everything in tier 2 plus the work of wiring the system to your real calendar and — this
is what actually costs money — guaranteeing that what it does is correct:
that it checks before promising, that it does not duplicate a booking when the customer
insists, that it undoes its own work if an operation fails halfway, and that it does not
fill in facts it does not have.

None of that work shows up in a demo. It shows up six months later, in the fact that you
have not had to check what it says.

## The four questions that separate one tier from another

Ask them of any quote, ours included. If the person selling cannot answer them
concretely, you are looking at tier 1 or 2 even when the price is tier 3:
- Does it check real availability before proposing a time, or does it only look
like it does?
- If a booking fails halfway, does it stay half-done or undo itself?
- Can it book the same appointment twice if the customer insists?
- When it does not know something, does it say so or make it up?

An answer along the lines of "that's handled in the prompt" is not a yes. It means they
have asked the model to behave, not that the behaviour is guaranteed. That is
the difference between an instruction that can be skipped on an odd day and a check that
runs every time.

## What about building it myself with automation tools?

It is the alternative most people consider, and it deserves an honest answer: for
mechanical tasks — when this arrives, send that — automation tools are excellent and
cheap.

The trouble starts when what is on the other end is a conversation. The data does not
arrive tidy or complete: it arrives in pieces, with changes of mind and questions in
between. And three costs are invisible at the start:
- The official WhatsApp API. Without it, sending reminders from an
ordinary number ends in a block. With it, you have to manage templates and the
24-hour window — covered in
WhatsApp Business vs API.
- Maintenance. Not building it, keeping it right: you change a price,
you add a service, a schedule shifts.
- The odd cases. Ninety per cent of conversations are easy. The
remaining ten per cent is where you lose the customer, and where the development time
goes.

It adds up if you have someone to maintain it and your volume is low. It stops adding up
the moment one mishandled booking costs you more than the price difference.

## The comparison almost nobody makes

The usual question is "is it expensive?". The useful one is "compared to what?".
- Against a person: a receptionist in Spain costs
€25,000 to €35,000 a year fully loaded — the figure varies by country,
but the shape of the comparison does not — and they take days off, get ill, and do not
cover nights or Sundays, which is when a good share of enquiries arrive.
- Against doing nothing: that is where the real cost sits, and it
appears on no invoice. The slots that go empty without warning, the 23:40 message
answered at 10:00 when that person has already written to three other places, and the
ones who ask the price and never come back.

### How many saved appointments cover the fee

At a €200 average ticket and a 65% contribution margin:

| | Monthly fee | Saved appointments/month that cover it

| €149 | 2

| €390 | 3

| €690 | 6

| €990 | 8

Note that this counts margin, not revenue. A €200 appointment is not
€200 of profit: it consumes product and consumables. Presenting gross revenue as
"savings" is the most common error in these calculations and the first thing anyone who
can read a set of accounts will spot.

You can run it on your own figures in the
ROI calculator: it is built to tell you it does not pay
for itself yet, and if that is the answer, it says so.

## What to check in the small print

Before signing, check these five points in any offer:
- What counts as a "conversation". If they count messages rather than
24-hour conversations, the same volume costs you five to ten times more.
- What happens if you exceed the limit. Is the excess billed, or is the
service cut off? A customer left unanswered for hitting a cap is the opposite of what
you bought.
- What maintenance covers. Changing a price or adding a service should
be inside it. If every change is billed, the real price is not the one you were
quoted.
- When setup is charged. The reasonable arrangement is that nothing is
paid until the trial ends and you decide to continue.
- Whether there is a lock-in. A product that works does not need one.

For reference, here are our numbers: setup from €290 to €1,690 depending on plan — under
two months of fee, and only if you continue — extra conversations at €0.25, extra minutes
at €0.20, no lock-in and no service cut-off when you pass the limit. Full plans on the
pricing section.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why do some charge €99 and others €690 for the same thing?

Because it is not the same thing. The €99 offer is usually a drawn flow that
cannot check your calendar; the €690 one checks real availability and executes the
booking. The question that separates them is not price, it is
"does it check before promising a time?".

### Are there free AI assistants for clinics?

There are free tiers of flow-builder tools, and they are fine for answering four
common questions. None of them book against your real calendar, because that
requires an integration that costs money to maintain. If what you need is to
inform, a free one may be enough.

### What does setup cost and why is it charged?

In our case €290 to €1,690 depending on the plan, always under two months of
fee. It is not a licence being switched on: someone loads your services, prices and
durations, connects your number and your calendar, configures your real opening
hours and trains your team. It is charged only if you continue after the trial, and
waived if you pay a quarter up front.

### What does building it myself cost?

On the open market, building a system that genuinely checks your calendar and
executes bookings runs €2,000 to €15,000. With automation tools you
can cut that initial figure a long way, but the real cost is not building it — it is
maintaining it and covering the odd cases.

### What counts as a conversation?

It should be one customer talking to you over 24 hours, not each
message. If someone sends thirty messages in an afternoon, that is one conversation,
not thirty. Worth asking explicitly, because it changes the real price by a factor of
five or ten.

### What if my average ticket is low?

Then you need more saved appointments to cover the fee, and the larger plan may
not pay for itself — or any of them may not. It is arithmetic, not an opinion: run it
on your figures in the calculator. If it says it does
not pay, it does not pay.

## Do the maths before you decide

Put in your ticket, your appointments and your real no-show rate and see what comes
out. And if you would rather watch it running on your own services and prices, the
demo is 20 minutes and costs nothing.

2018 Toyota Camry

Title: AI receptionist for hair restoration and laser clinics | Hachi

# AI receptionist for hair restoration and laser clinics

A hair transplant is decided slowly and paid for dearly; laser hair removal is six or seven spaced sessions. Both depend on answering the first message fast and not losing anyone between one session and the next.

For businesses in the United States

## What you lose today

### The expensive lead nobody answers

An ad lead for a transplant costs real money. If it takes a day to get a reply, that money is wasted.

### Sessions that drift

Laser works when the intervals are kept. A client who does not book the next session in time loses results and ends up unhappy.

### The decision that cools off

Someone asking about a transplant thinks about it for weeks. Without follow-up, the conversation stops at the price.

## How Hachi answers

Daniel · WhatsApp · 12:14 am

Hey, how much for a hair transplant? Sending you a pic of where I'm at

📷 Photo

Hi, Luna is due for her rabies shot, anything this week?

Hi Ashley! For Luna's rabies vaccine I have Thursday at 10:30 am or Friday at 6:00 pm. Which works better?

Friday

All set: Luna, rabies vaccine, Friday at 6:00 pm. Please bring her vaccination records. I'll text you a reminder on Thursday.

Nobody on the team stepped in

If Ashley had written "Luna is vomiting blood", the conversation would have gone to a person on the team at that moment, without touching the calendar.

## What Hachi does for a vet clinic
- Asks for the pet's name and species before booking, because it is set up with the details your clinic needs.
- Books exams, vaccines, scheduled surgery or grooming, each with its own length and provider.
- SMS reminders before each visit; the next dose can be booked when the current one ends.
- Recognises an emergency (ingestion, wounds, trouble breathing) and hands it to a person instantly.
- Answers the phone with voice when the team cannot, and replies to Spanish-speaking pet owners in Spanish.

## What the code prevents in a vet clinic

The model understands and converses; the critical rules are enforced by code (the guardrails), whatever the conversation says. The ones that matter most here:

It does not lose an emergency. A message describing an emergency is escalated to a person, even if something fails internally. Here that comes first.

It does not double-book. Even if the owner insists or sends the details across several messages, the vaccine is booked once.

It does not confirm a taken slot. It checks the vet's calendar before offering a time.

## When does it pay for itself?

With an average ticket of $150 and a 55% contribution margin (an example assumption), the Professional plan pays for itself with 10 saved appointments a month. We count margin, not revenue: an appointment is not all profit.

Run it with your own numbers in the calculator: it can tell you it does not pay off yet, and if so, it says so.

## Which plan fits

Professional

$809/mo · $1,399 one-off setup

A vet clinic runs on the phone, and voice starts on the Professional plan: 400 minutes a month, calendars for each vet and for grooming, and WhatsApp calls.

A small clinic can start on Essential and add voice as an add-on.

Prices for the United States, in USD. Pay-per-booking $59 + $5 per booking, Solo $179, Essential $459, Professional $809 and Complete $1,159 a month. Reminders and follow-ups go out by SMS or WhatsApp, whichever your clients use.

Before paying anything: a 20-minute demo and a 7-day trial with your assistant already set up, no card. No lock-in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does HIPAA apply to a vet clinic?

No. HIPAA protects human health information; animal records are not covered. You still have privacy obligations toward the owners' personal data, and Hachi keeps each clinic's data isolated from every other.

### Can it give veterinary advice?

No, and it is set up not to. It informs with what you give it (hours, prices, pre-surgery instructions) and, for any symptom, books an exam or hands the conversation to a person.

### Does it remind owners about the next vaccine?

It sends a reminder for every booked appointment by SMS or WhatsApp. If the next dose is booked when the current one ends, the reminder goes out on its own.

### What happens with an emergency at night?

The conversation is flagged as urgent and goes to your team. If you have an on-call number or a partner emergency hospital, it is set up to give it.
